title: Projects
text: My first research rotation as a Ph.D. student involved recoding qualitative data from the 2025 Cleveland Health Survey. This was an iterative process during which I developed a new codebook that can be used for future Cleveland Health Surveys or to conduct preliminary exploratory analysis of the 2025 data. This was a ten-week process that gave me a deeper understanding of the issues that Cleveland residents face in their communities, as described in their own words.

title: Projects
section: Role of the Rfa2 winged-helix domain
text:
Role of the Rfa2 winged-helix domain
During a semester as a student and researcher with Dr. Alex Pike at Oberlin College, I performed molecular biology experiments to mutate the winged-helix domain of the Rfa2 protein in S. cerevisiae and test cellular response to DNA damage from UV light. Results were used to support hypothesis testing surrounding the role that the winged-helix domain plays in DNA damage response, an important pathway to understand for cancer research.

title: Projects
section: QSAR model predicting ligand compatibility with prostate-specific membrane antigen
text:
QSAR model predicting ligand compatibility with prostate-specific membrane antigen
As a computational biology research assistant to Dr. Zahra Nikfarjam, I used software like LeDock and AutoDock to simulate the binding of various ligands to the prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). Ligands were synthesized using prior literature on PSMA ligand structures and pharmacokinetic properties, then altering the ligand composition to maximize fit. The results of docking simulations were used to refine a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) model.

title: Asha Agarwal
text:
Hello and welcome to my website! My name is Asha Agarwal and I am a first-year Epidemiology and Biostatistics Ph.D. student at the Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine. I am located within the Population and Quantitative Health Department, where we study, model, and design interventions to address health outcomes among populations on the local all the way to the global level.
I am interested in using community-engaged methods to address the health outcomes of adolescents and predominantly immigrant or minority communities. I am learning about mixed-methods approaches, community-based participatory research, and intervention science—primarily in the context of the greater Cleveland community. Through my research rotations, I will be learning under the mentorship of Dr. Jin Kim-Mozeleski, Dr. Erika Trapl, and Dr. Fredrick Schumacher.
